text:
mia: heads up — after last rollout charts are stuttering on console when switching teams, especially heatmaps. noticed on both prod and staging. :frowning_face:

sam: saw this too. heatmap paint jumps ~400-800ms on first open, subsequent opens still slow (~200ms).

ash: bundle analyzer shows a chunk bump from the recent chart refactor. `main+charts` went from ~5.2MB to 6.9MB after the PR. probable culprit is new dependency `super-heatmap-ux` pulled in heavy color-scale code.

jordan: telemetry confirms spike: charts render latency percentile P95 moved from 120ms -> 570ms for users in eu-west1 since deployment. also increased number of GETs to `/api/console/metrics` per page load.

mia: thanks. could be two issues: bundle size + extra network roundtrips. any idea why `/api/console/metrics` is being requested twice? we didn't change client code to call it twice.

sam: routing policy change last week added a metrics proxy for quotas check. proxy adds an extra redirect/forward. it was supposed to be a background call but is now blocking chart render due to how we await data in ChartLoader.

ash: yup — look at ChartLoader: `await fetchMetrics()` is inside the component init path. should be async-suspended so render doesn't block. quick patch: move metrics fetch to `useEffect` and let chart show cached placeholders.

jordan: also found a KV cache key mismatch. telemetry shows cache miss ratio ~92% for heatmap tile responses. the key includes `teamId` but our rollout renamed `teamId` -> `team.id` in the request payload, so cache keys never hit.

mia: of course. that explains the backend load too. high miss rate means charts re-fetch raw data and re-compute heavy color scales on each open. :facepalm:

sam: proposed fixes (short list):
- revert heavy color-scale dependency and lazy-load it via dynamic import
- change ChartLoader to render skeleton, move metrics fetch into effect (non-blocking)
- patch cache key generation to normalize `teamId/team.id` and add fallback TTL bump for warmup
- add small client-side LRU cache for heatmap tiles to avoid backend trips on quick tab switches

ash: code snippet for lazy-load: `const HeatmapLib = () => import('super-heatmap-ux')` (or `const Heatmap = dynamic(() => import('super-heatmap-ux'), { ssr: false })` for Next). reduces initial bytes.

jordan: for the proxy routing: need to change policy so quota-check runs on a non-blocking worker route, or respond with cached quota and update in background. current deploy changed `route: blocking` accidentally. PR incoming to change to `route: background` in routing table.

mia: good. can someone put together a small rollout plan? we need quick mitigation then proper fix: 1) hotfix cache key + move metrics to useEffect (patch -> canary), 2) revert/ lazy-load heavy lib (patch 2), 3) routing policy change (config rollback), 4) follow-up perf test and telemetry dashboard.

sam: I'll open hotfix PRs for cache key and ChartLoader change now. marking as high priority.

ash: I'll draft bundle rollback + lazy-load PR. also add webpack split for color-scale into separate chunk with `/* webpackChunkName: "color-scale" */`.

jordan: I'll update telemetry dashboard: add P50/P95 charts per region and cache hit ratio panel so we can watch after canary. also add a synthetic test that opens heatmap and measures interactive paint.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: staging-hotfix -> approved by mia. deploy-ids: deploy-stg-1835-hotfix-1. ETA ~7m.

mia: thanks all. after staging validation let's canary to 10% in prod and watch the new panels. keep slack updates short. :thumbsup:

sam: quick note — adding a small client LRU (in-memory) may cause memory thrash for users with many tabs. I'll limit to 6 tiles per tab and 30s TTL.

ash: ok pushed the webpack split suggestion to PR description. also removed one large transitive dependency (color-utils) that was only used for dev-time gradients — saved ~300KB gzipped.

jordan: telemetry now shows staging P95 down to ~180ms after hotfix deploy. cache hit ratio jumped to 64% (was 8%). will monitor.

mia: excellent. leave this thread with status updates. we'll do postmortem if prod shows anything odd after canary.
